text:
Maya: Heads-up — noticed a bunch of SLO alerts this morning tied to model endpoints in eu-west1. Latency spikes right after scale-to-zero events. Anyone else seeing long cold-starts for GPU nodes?
Liam: Yep saw it. GPUS are taking ~90-120s to be ready from node creation, then another ~10-20s for pods + container runtime.
Joan: That's expected for that instance type in eu-west1, boot + driver + nvidia setup. Warm pool seems like our best option if we want <30s tail latency.
Maya: Agree. Current policy: scale-to-zero after 5m idle, cooldown 2m. That looks aggressive.
Frank: Cost note — we've been charged for ~120 idle GPU-hours last week across eu-west1 and us-central when we kept warm pools at 1 instance. Tradeoff math matters. I can share a quick calc.
Maya: Can we try a different approach: node warm pool size=0 but keep one preemptible 4-GPU node in warm pool during business hours? @Liam thoughts?
Liam: That'd reduce cold starts but preemptible brings churn. Maybe keep 1 non-preemptible in eu-west1 during 08:00-20:00 local, fallback outside hours. Also raise scale-down cooldown to 15m.
Sean: +1 on 15m. Also suggest tune cluster-autoscaler scale-down-unneeded-time and scale-down-unready-time. Our current flags: 
```
--scale-down-unneeded-time=5m
--scale-down-unready-time=10m
--max-node-provision-time=15m
```
Those are too tight for GPUs.
Joan: We should also consider warm-pool lifecycle: ensure k8s node labels are applied before workloads land. I hit races where kubelet finishes after workload scheduling. Add a readiness gate?
OpsBot: Autoscaler event: 1747854500 scale_up: request for 8 gpus in eu-west1 triggered. reason: pending pod 3 (model-inference).
Frank: Proposed config snippet for testing: 
```yaml
nodePools:
  - name: gpu-warmpool-1
    size: 1
    preemptible: false
    zones: [eu-west1-b, eu-west1-c]
    warmPool: true
    cooldown: 15m
    labels: {role: gpu-warm}
```
Maya: That looks good. Can we limit warm pool to a single zone to reduce cross-zone startup variance? Joan?
Joan: Single zone reduces some risk but increases outage blast radius. If we pick eu-west1-b it's the most stable historically. Also add node taint so regular pods don't use it except inference.
Liam: For autoscaler flags, let's try: 
```
--scale-down-unneeded-time=20m
--scale-down-unready-time=30m
--max-node-provision-time=25m
```
And ensure the autoscaler respects node group protected-size for warm pool.
Frank: I'll run cost simulation: keep 1 dedicated warm node from 08:00-20:00, rest scale-to-zero. If preemptible is okay we can test next week on a/cost branch.
Sean: Also add metric to detect user-facing tail latency during cold starts: synthetic p95 burst test every hour that forces scale-up and logs time to first token.
Maya: Action items: Frank = cost sim and compare preemptible vs reserved; Liam = deploy autoscaler flag changes to staging; Joan = propose zone/taint policy and handle readiness gating; Sean = implement synthetic p95 test. I'll schedule a quick sync after data comes in. :+1:
Liam: I'll push a rollout with the new flags to staging today and add feature flag to toggle warm-pool.
Joan: One more gotcha — network CNI initialization can also add 10-30s on some nodes. If we pre-pull driver/container image to warm nodes that saves time.
Maya: Good call. Pre-pull image + host driver preload in warm pool.
OpsBot: Deployment note: 1747855600 rollout gpu-autoscaler-flags -> staging succeeded.
Frank: Posting cost sim once done. Thanks all.
Maya: Thanks team. We'll reconvene after metrics. :wave:
